easy.def: A person who tells lies.
examples: No one trusts a liar.
The boy was called a liar.
A liar does not tell the truth.

more.def: A person who does not tell the truth.
examples: Nobody believed the liar.
In the story, a liar told tall tales.
The liar was caught in his lie.

easy.def: To set someone free.
examples: They liberated the bird.
The soldiers liberated the town.
We liberate the fish from the net.

more.def: To set someone or something free from a place or from the control of others.
examples: The children liberated the butterfly from the jar and watched it fly away.
The army liberated the town from the cruel ruler.
The gardener liberated the tree from the tangled vines.

easy.def: Freedom.
examples: The statue stands for liberty.
People want liberty.
Liberty is important.

more.def: The freedom to live and make choices without being controlled by others.
examples: The Statue of Liberty stands in New York harbor.
The people fought for their liberty.
Liberty means you can choose your own way.

easy.def: A person who works in a library.
examples: The librarian found me a book.
Our librarian reads us stories.
I asked the librarian for help.

more.def: A person whose job is to take care of a library and help people find books and information.
examples: The librarian showed us where to find books about space.
Our school librarian reads a story to the class every Friday.
I asked the librarian to help me look up facts about frogs.

easy.def: A place with lots of books you can borrow.
examples: I got a book from the library.
The library is a quiet place.
Our school has a library.

more.def: A place where books and other materials are kept for people to read or borrow.
examples: We go to the library every Saturday to choose new books.
You need a card to borrow books from the library.
The library offers story time for young children.

easy.def: A paper that says you may do something.
examples: Dad has a driver's license.
You need a fishing license.
The license is in his wallet.

more.def: An official card or paper that says a person is allowed to do something.
examples: Aunt Rosa has a license to fly planes.
You need a license to go fishing.
The dog's license hangs on its collar.

easy.def: To move your tongue over something.
examples: The dog licks my face.
I lick the spoon.
She licked her ice cream.

more.def: To pass your tongue over something.
examples: The dog licked my hand.
She licked the ice cream cone.
The cat licked its paw clean.

easy.def: A black or red chewy candy.
examples: I like licorice.
The licorice is chewy.
She ate a licorice.

more.def: A chewy candy with a strong taste, often black or red.
examples: I chewed a red licorice twist.
The black licorice had a strong taste.
She gave me a piece of licorice.

easy.def: A cover for a pot or box.
examples: Put the lid on.
The lid is tight.
The pot has a lid.

more.def: A cover that fits over the top of a container.
examples: Put the lid on the jar.
The lid on the pot rattled.
I lost the lid to my lunch box.

easy.def: Something you say that is not true.
examples: That is a lie.
He told a lie.
A lie is not okay.

more.def: A statement that a person knows is not true.
examples: It was a lie when he said he did not break the vase.
She felt bad after telling a lie to her friend.
The wolf in the story told a lie about the sheep.

easy.def: To rest flat on the ground or a bed.
examples: I lie on the grass.
The cat lay in the sun.
Lie down and rest.

more.def: To rest in a flat position on a surface.
examples: We lay on the grass and watched the clouds float by.
The baby lies on a blanket during the day.
Please lie down if you feel dizzy.

easy.def: A leader of a small group of soldiers.
examples: The lieutenant led the group.
A lieutenant gave orders.
The lieutenant saluted.

more.def: A military officer of middle rank, below a captain.
examples: The lieutenant led her team across the field.
A lieutenant gave orders to the soldiers.
The lieutenant is one rank below captain.

easy.def: The time from when you are born until you die.
examples: My grandpa had a long life.
A pet's life is short.
She has a happy life.

more.def: The state of being alive, or the time that a person or animal is alive.
examples: Plants and animals are living things, and they all have life.
A tortoise can have a very long life.
Scientists study life in the ocean.

easy.def: A small boat used to save people from a ship.
examples: Everyone got in the lifeboat.
The ship had lifeboats.
The lifeboat saved us.

more.def: A small boat that is kept on a ship or at the shore and used to rescue people in danger.
examples: Each ship carries lifeboats in case of an emergency.
The lifeboat went out to rescue the sailors.
We learned how to get into the lifeboat on the cruise.

easy.def: A person who watches swimmers to keep them safe.
examples: The lifeguard watches the pool.
A lifeguard blew a whistle.
The lifeguard saved a swimmer.

more.def: A person whose job is to watch swimmers at a beach or pool and rescue anyone who is in trouble.
examples: The lifeguard sat in a tall chair watching the swimmers.
A lifeguard blew a whistle and told us to stay out of the deep end.
The lifeguard swam out to help the tired swimmer.

easy.def: Without life, or dull.
examples: The planet was lifeless.
A lifeless desert lay ahead.
The doll lay lifeless.

more.def: Without life, or without energy and interest.
examples: The dry desert looked lifeless under the sun.
The lifeless doll lay on the shelf.
His lifeless voice made the story dull.

easy.def: Looking real.
examples: The doll is lifelike.
A lifelike statue.
The painting is lifelike.

more.def: Looking very real or like something alive.
examples: The doll looked so lifelike that I stared.
The artist made a lifelike statue.
The lifelike painting seemed to move.

easy.def: A rope or help that keeps you safe.
examples: The rope was a lifeline.
The phone is a lifeline.
Throw him a lifeline.

more.def: A rope used to save someone, or something you depend on in time of need.
examples: The sailor threw a lifeline to the swimmer.
The radio was their lifeline during the storm.
A friend's kind words were a lifeline to her.

easy.def: Lasting for your whole life.
examples: A lifelong friend.
A lifelong dream.
A lifelong habit.

more.def: Lasting for the whole of a person's life.
examples: She has been my lifelong friend since we were babies.
His lifelong dream was to fly an airplane.
Reading is a lifelong habit.

easy.def: A person or thing that helps in a very important way.
examples: You are a lifesaver!
The map was a lifesaver.
The snack was a lifesaver.

more.def: A person or thing that helps you in a time of need, or a person who saves people from drowning.
examples: The umbrella was a lifesaver in the rain.
Thanks for the ride, you are a lifesaver.
The lifesaver at the pool pulled the child to safety.

easy.def: The way you live.
examples: She has a healthy lifestyle.
The lifestyle is busy.
They have a quiet lifestyle.

more.def: The way that a person or family lives each day.
examples: She has a healthy lifestyle and exercises daily.
They have a quiet lifestyle in the country.
A busy lifestyle can be tiring.

easy.def: All the years someone is alive.
examples: She read many books in her lifetime.
A lifetime is a long time.
Dogs live shorter lifetimes than people.

more.def: The whole length of time that a person or thing lives.
examples: Grandma saw many changes in her lifetime.
The tortoise's lifetime can be over a hundred years.
A butterfly's lifetime is only a few weeks.

easy.def: To pick something up.
examples: Lift the box.
I lifted my arm.
He lifts the bag.

more.def: To raise something to a higher place.
examples: She lifted the heavy box.
He lifted his little sister onto the bench.
The crane lifts steel beams.

easy.def: A ride in a car.
examples: Can I get a lift?
Dad gave me a lift to school.
We got a lift home.

more.def: A ride in someone's car.
examples: Can you give me a lift to the game?
A neighbor gave us a lift to the store.
She got a lift home after practice.

easy.def: A person or thing that lifts.
examples: The lifter raised the box.
A weight lifter is strong.
The lifter is a machine.

more.def: A person or machine that lifts things.
examples: The weight lifter raised the bar over his head.
A machine lifter moved the heavy crates.
The lifter in the warehouse was busy.

easy.def: When a rocket leaves the ground.
examples: The liftoff was loud.
We watched the liftoff.
Liftoff is at noon.

more.def: The moment when a rocket or spacecraft leaves the ground.
examples: We watched the rocket's liftoff on TV.
Liftoff happened at noon.
The crowd cheered at liftoff.

easy.def: What lets you see.
examples: Turn on the light.
The sun gives light.
A light is on.

more.def: The brightness from the sun, a lamp, or fire that makes it possible to see.
examples: Light from the sun takes about eight minutes to reach Earth.
She turned on the light so she could read.
The light from the candle flickered in the dark room.

easy.def: Not heavy.
examples: The bag is light.
A feather is light.
This box is light.

more.def: Not heavy, or easy to lift or carry.
examples: The kite is light enough to float on the breeze.
I packed a light jacket for the cool evening.
A feather is so light that the wind carries it away.

related.def: Being light, not heavy or not dark.

easy.def: A glass bulb that gives light.
examples: The lightbulb is bright.
I changed a lightbulb.
The lightbulb burned out.

more.def: A glass bulb that gives off light when electricity passes through it.
examples: Dad changed the lightbulb in the lamp.
A lightbulb hung from the ceiling by a long cord.
A lightbulb glowed above the table.

easy.def: To make lighter.
examples: The paint will lighten.
We lightened the load.
The sky lightened.

more.def: To make something less heavy or less dark.
examples: We lightened the load by taking out the books.
The sky lightened at dawn.
A joke lightened the mood.

easy.def: A tall tower with a bright light that guides ships.
examples: The lighthouse shines at night.
A lighthouse is by the sea.
We saw a lighthouse.

more.def: A tall tower by the sea with a bright light on top that warns and guides ships.
examples: The lighthouse light shone across the water.
A keeper once lived in the lighthouse by the rocks.
Ships use the lighthouse to stay safe at night.

easy.def: The lights in a place.
examples: The lighting is soft.
The lighting is bright.
The stage lighting is red.

more.def: The lights that are used in a place, or the way a place is lit.
examples: The soft lighting made the room cozy.
The stage lighting was bright red.
We need better lighting to read.

easy.def: In a soft or gentle way.
examples: The snow fell lightly.
She touched it lightly.
He tapped lightly on the door.

more.def: With little force or weight.
examples: A little snow fell lightly on the grass.
She lightly touched the sleeping baby.
He tapped lightly on the window.

easy.def: A bright flash of light in the sky in a storm.
examples: I saw lightning and then heard thunder.
Lightning hit the tall tree.
The lightning was so bright.

more.def: A bright flash of electricity in the sky during a storm.
examples: Lightning lit up the whole sky for a second.
Never stand under a tree when there is lightning.
We counted the seconds between the lightning and the thunder.

easy.def: Not heavy.
examples: The bag is lightweight.
I have a lightweight coat.
The toy is lightweight.

more.def: Weighing very little.
examples: The lightweight jacket was easy to pack.
She carried a lightweight tent on the hike.
The lightweight plastic cup floated on the water.

easy.def: Easy to like.
examples: The puppy is likable.
He is a likable boy.
She is a likable teacher.

more.def: Pleasant and easy to like.
examples: The new boy was friendly and likable.
She is a likable character in the story.
The shy but likable puppy made friends fast.

easy.def: To think something is nice and enjoy it.
examples: I like apples.
She likes to dance.
We liked the movie.

more.def: To enjoy something or to think well of someone or something.
examples: My brother likes to build models of airplanes.
Do you like the new teacher?
We liked the zoo so much that we visited again.

easy.def: The same as, or almost the same as.
examples: He runs like the wind.
You look like your mom.
It feels like silk.

more.def: Similar to something, or in the same way as something.
examples: The clouds looked like cotton balls floating in the sky.
She sings like a bird, with a clear and sweet voice.
A zebra looks like a horse with stripes.

easy.def: How likely something is.
examples: There is a likelihood of rain.
The likelihood is small.
What is the likelihood of snow?

more.def: The chance that something will happen.
examples: There is a high likelihood of rain tomorrow.
The likelihood of finding a four-leaf clover is small.
With such dark clouds, the likelihood of a picnic was low.

easy.def: Having a good chance to happen.
examples: It is likely to rain.
She is likely to win.
He is likely to be late.

more.def: Having a good chance of happening or being true.
examples: It is likely to snow tonight, so bring a coat.
The team is likely to win after such a good practice.
A cloudy sky makes rain more likely.

easy.def: A way that two things look alike.
examples: There is a likeness between them.
The picture is a good likeness.
The likeness is clear.

more.def: The way that two people or things look the same, or a picture of someone.
examples: There is a strong likeness between the sisters.
The painting was a good likeness of my grandfather.
The statue is a perfect likeness of the queen.

easy.def: In the same way.
examples: I like cake, and likewise my sister.
He waved, and I did likewise.
Do likewise.

more.def: In the same way, or also.
examples: She smiled at us, and we did likewise.
Mom said thank you, and Dad did likewise.
Watch how I do it, then do likewise.

easy.def: A bush with sweet-smelling purple flowers.
examples: The lilac smells sweet.
We picked a lilac.
The lilac is purple.

more.def: A bush with clusters of sweet-smelling pale purple or white flowers.
examples: The lilac in our yard smells sweet in spring.
Mom put lilacs in a vase.
Bees buzzed around the lilac bush.

easy.def: A big flower shaped like a bell.
examples: A lily grew by the pond.
The lily smells nice.
I gave Mom a lily.

more.def: A tall plant with large, trumpet-shaped flowers that smell sweet.
examples: The pond was covered with lily pads and one white lily.
Lilies come in many colors, such as white, pink and orange.
She planted lily bulbs in the garden in the fall.

easy.def: An arm, a leg or a branch.
examples: The tree limb is big.
I broke a limb.
The limb fell.

more.def: A part of the body such as an arm or leg, or a big branch of a tree.
examples: A tree limb fell in the storm.
Your arms and legs are limbs.
The bird sat on a high limb.

easy.def: Able to bend and move easily.
examples: The dancer is limber.
I saw a limber cat.
She is limber.

more.def: Able to bend and move easily.
examples: The limber gymnast bent over backwards.
The cat is limber and can squeeze through gaps.
He stretched to stay limber.

easy.def: A dance where you bend back to go under a low bar.
examples: We did the limbo.
The limbo is a game.
She won the limbo.

more.def: A party game and dance in which people bend backward to pass under a low bar, or a state of waiting where nothing is decided yet.
examples: At the party, we played the limbo and bent under the stick.
She was in limbo waiting to hear if she got the part.
The bar went lower and lower in the limbo contest.

easy.def: A small, round green fruit that tastes sour.
examples: I squeezed a lime.
The lime is green.
We put lime in the drink.

more.def: A small, round, green fruit with sour juice, used in drinks and food.
examples: I squeezed lime juice into the water.
A slice of lime sat on the side of the glass.
The lime tree in the yard has bright green fruit.

easy.def: A gray or white rock.
examples: The cliff is limestone.
Limestone is a rock.
The walls are limestone.

more.def: A hard gray or white rock used for building and made from shells and bones of tiny sea animals.
examples: Caves often form in limestone.
The old castle was built of limestone.
Chalk is a soft kind of limestone.

easy.def: The top amount you can have.
examples: The speed limit is twenty-five.
There is a limit of two cookies.
The limit is five.

more.def: The point beyond which something may not go.
examples: The speed limit near the school is twenty miles per hour.
There is a limit of two cookies each.
The bridge has a weight limit.

easy.def: To keep something from going past a certain point.
examples: We limit our screen time.
The teacher limited us to five minutes.
Dad limits sweets.

more.def: To keep something within a certain amount.
examples: Parents often limit the time kids spend on screens.
The coach limited practice to one hour.
We limit ourselves to one cookie each.

easy.def: Something that stops you from doing more.
examples: Money is a limitation.
There is a limitation on time.
Every machine has limitations.

more.def: A rule, a fact or a weakness that stops a person or a thing from doing more.
examples: The small size of the boat was a limitation, so only four people could ride.
There is a limitation on how many books you can borrow at once.
Knowing your own limitations helps you to ask for help.

easy.def: Not much, or small in number.
examples: We have limited time.
Space is limited.
The seats are limited.

more.def: Small in amount, size or number.
examples: We have limited time before the bus comes.
The room has limited space for chairs.
Supplies are limited, so please take only one.

easy.def: With no end.
examples: Her energy is limitless.
A limitless sky.
The ideas are limitless.

more.def: Having no limit or end.
examples: The sky seemed limitless.
Her energy seemed limitless.
His imagination is limitless.

easy.def: A long, fancy car.
examples: The limo is long.
We rode in a limo.
The singer arrived in a limo.

more.def: A short word for limousine, a long, fancy car.
examples: The singer arrived in a black limo.
We rode in a limo to the wedding.
The long limo parked at the door.

easy.def: A very long, fancy car.
examples: The singer rode in a limousine.
A black limousine waited outside.
We saw a long limousine.

more.def: A very long, fancy car with a driver, often used for special events like weddings or big parties.
examples: The bride and groom left the wedding in a white limousine.
A shiny limousine pulled up in front of the theater.
The class laughed at the idea of riding to school in a limousine.

easy.def: To walk in an uneven way.
examples: He limps.
The dog limped.
I limped home.

more.def: To walk in an uneven way because of a hurt leg or foot.
examples: The dog limped on its sore paw.
He limped off the field.
I limped home with a sore ankle.

easy.def: Soft and not stiff.
examples: The flower is limp.
The lettuce is limp.
A limp handshake.

more.def: Soft and floppy, not firm or stiff.
examples: The flowers were limp from the heat.
The lettuce went limp in the sun.
He gave a limp wave.

easy.def: In a weak, soft way.
examples: The flower hung limply.
His arm hung limply.
She held it limply.

more.def: In a weak way, without strength or firmness.
examples: The flag hung limply on the pole because there was no wind.
His arm hung limply at his side.
The wet towel lay limply on the chair.

easy.def: A long, thin mark.
examples: Draw a line.
She drew a straight line.
The line is long.

more.def: A long, thin mark, or something that looks like one.
examples: Use a ruler to draw a straight line across the page.
A line of ants marched across the sidewalk.
The line on the road shows where to drive.

easy.def: People standing one behind the other.
examples: Stand in line.
The line is long.
We wait in line.

more.def: A row of people or things waiting, one behind the other.
examples: We stood in line to buy ice cream.
The children made a line at the classroom door.
A long line of cars waited at the bridge.

easy.def: A football player who tries to stop the other team.
examples: The linebacker tackled.
A linebacker is strong.
He is a linebacker.

more.def: A player on a football team who stands behind the front line to stop the other team.
examples: The linebacker stopped the runner.
A linebacker has to be fast and strong.
He plays linebacker for the high school team.

easy.def: Soft, light cloth for sheets and shirts.
examples: The tablecloth is made of linen.
A linen shirt keeps you cool.
Linen is soft.

more.def: A cloth made from the flax plant that is light and cool, used for clothes and household items.
examples: The tablecloth was made of white linen.
A linen shirt keeps you cool on a hot day.
Sheets and towels are sometimes called bed and bath linens.

easy.def: A thing that covers the inside of something.
examples: A liner for the trash can.
The liner is plastic.
The coat has a liner.

more.def: Something that covers the inside of a container or a garment, or a large ship that carries passengers.
examples: Put a new liner in the trash can.
The coat has a warm liner inside it.
The ocean liner carried passengers across the sea.

easy.def: A list of the players who will take part in a game.
examples: The coach read the lineup.
I am in the lineup today.
Our lineup has nine players.

more.def: A list or row of the players or performers who will take part in a game or show.
examples: The coach read out the lineup before the baseball game.
The band's lineup for the concert had five singers.
She was glad to be in the starting lineup.

easy.def: To stay a little longer.
examples: The smell lingered.
We lingered at the park.
Don't linger.

more.def: To stay somewhere longer than needed, or to last a long time.
examples: We lingered at the park until the sun went down.
The smell of cookies lingered in the kitchen.
She lingered at the door and waved goodbye.

easy.def: The special words used by a group.
examples: I learned the lingo.
Sailors have their own lingo.
The lingo was new to me.

more.def: The special words and way of speaking used by a certain group.
examples: Sailors have their own lingo for parts of a ship.
Gamers use lingo that other people may not know.
I learned the lingo of the baseball team.

easy.def: A layer of material on the inside of something.
examples: My coat has a warm lining.
The box has a soft lining.
The lining is red.

more.def: A layer of material that covers the inside of something, such as a coat, a bag or a box.
examples: The silk lining of the coat felt smooth against my arms.
A soft lining kept the jewelry from getting scratched.
The lining of the stomach is made of tiny cells.

easy.def: One ring in a chain.
examples: The chain has a broken link.
Each link is made of metal.
I counted the links.

more.def: One of the rings or parts that join together to make a chain.
examples: One link in the chain was broken.
The links of the necklace were gold.
Each link in the bicycle chain is made of metal.

easy.def: A word you click to go to another page.
examples: Click the link.
The link takes you to a game.
She sent me a link.

more.def: A word or picture on a web page that you click to go to another page.
examples: Click the link to read more about whales.
The teacher sent us a link to a video.
There is a link at the bottom of the page.

easy.def: A smooth floor covering.
examples: The floor is linoleum.
The linoleum is shiny.
The linoleum is easy to clean.

more.def: A smooth, hard floor covering that is easy to wash.
examples: The kitchen floor is covered with linoleum.
The linoleum was shiny and easy to mop.
We slid across the linoleum in our socks.

easy.def: Tiny bits of fluff from cloth.
examples: There is lint on my shirt.
The dryer has lint.
I picked lint off my sweater.

more.def: Tiny bits of fluff from cloth that gather on clothes or in a dryer.
examples: Dad cleaned the lint out of the dryer.
There was lint in my pocket.
A roller picks up lint from the dark jacket.

easy.def: A big wild cat that roars.
examples: The lion roared.
A male lion has a mane.
Lions live in groups.

more.def: A large wild cat with golden fur, found in Africa, where the male has a thick mane.
examples: The lion lay in the shade of a tree.
Lions live in groups called prides.
A lion's roar can be heard from miles away.

easy.def: A female lion.
examples: The lioness has cubs.
A lioness hunts.
The lioness rested in the shade.

more.def: A grown-up female lion, which does most of the hunting for the group.
examples: The lioness crept through the tall grass toward a herd of zebras.
A lioness carried her cub gently in her mouth.
Lionesses live together in a family group called a pride.

easy.def: The soft edge of your mouth.
examples: She licked her lip.
My lips are dry.
He bit his lip.

more.def: One of the two soft edges around the opening of the mouth.
examples: She licked her lips.
My lips were chapped from the cold.
He pressed his lips together.

easy.def: A color that people put on their lips.
examples: She wore red lipstick.
The lipstick is pink.
Mom put on lipstick.

more.def: A waxy stick of color that is put on the lips.
examples: She put on pink lipstick.
The actor wore red lipstick on stage.
Mom put the lipstick in her bag.

easy.def: Something wet that you can pour.
examples: Water and milk are liquids.
Juice is a liquid.
The soap is a blue liquid.

more.def: Something that flows and can be poured, like water. It is not a solid or a gas.
examples: When ice melts, it changes from a solid into a liquid.
Honey is a thick liquid that pours slowly.
The nurse measured the liquid medicine in a spoon.

easy.def: Words or things in a row, one after another.
examples: Make a list.
My shopping list is long.
There is a list of names.

more.def: A series of names, items or numbers written one after another.
examples: I made a list of things to pack for camp.
Her name is first on the list.
Mom wrote a long grocery list.

easy.def: To write things in order.
examples: List your favorite foods.
She listed the planets.
He listed three reasons.

more.def: To write or say things one after another.
examples: Please list five animals that live in the sea.
She listed the planets in order from the sun.
He listed his favorite foods.

easy.def: To use your ears to hear.
examples: Listen to the birds sing.
I listen to music.
Please listen to the story.

more.def: To pay attention so that you can hear something.
examples: If you listen closely, you can hear the ocean from here.
We listened to the rain on the roof.
A good friend listens when you have a problem.

easy.def: A person who listens.
examples: She is a good listener.
The listener sat still.
Every listener clapped.

more.def: A person who pays attention to what someone says or to sounds such as music or a radio show.
examples: A good listener looks at you and waits for you to finish talking.
The radio host thanked every listener for calling in.
The storyteller smiled at her young listeners.

easy.def: A bit more than four cups of liquid.
examples: We bought a liter of juice.
The bottle holds one liter.
I drank a liter of water.

more.def: A unit for measuring liquid in the metric system, a little more than a quart.
examples: We bought a one-liter bottle of juice for the picnic.
The fish tank holds about forty liters of water.
A liter is the same as a thousand milliliters.

easy.def: Meaning exactly what the words say.
examples: The literal meaning is plain.
Take the words as literal.
It is a literal translation.

more.def: Following the exact meaning of the words, not a figure of speech.
examples: The literal meaning of "raining cats and dogs" is silly.
The book gave a literal translation of each word.
He took her joke in a literal way and looked for the cat.

easy.def: Exactly as the words say.
examples: The pizza was literally a mile wide.
It literally rained for a week.
He literally jumped for joy.

more.def: In the exact meaning of the words, without any exaggeration.
examples: The sign literally says "stop."
He literally jumped for joy, right into the air.
The soup was literally boiling when I took it off the stove.

easy.def: About books and writing.
examples: She likes literary things.
A literary club.
It is a literary prize.

more.def: Having to do with books and writing, especially good writing.
examples: She joined a literary club that meets at the library.
The author won a literary prize.
The town held a literary festival.

easy.def: Books and stories.
examples: We study literature.
She loves literature.
Literature class is fun.

more.def: Writing that is thought to be of high quality, such as novels, poems and plays.
examples: We read a poem in literature class.
She loves classic literature.
Children's literature has many wonderful stories.

easy.def: Trash left on the ground.
examples: Pick up the litter.
The park has litter.
Do not leave litter.

more.def: Trash and bits of garbage that are left lying about in a public place.
examples: We picked up litter at the park.
Litter on the beach harms animals.
Please put your litter in the bin.

easy.def: A group of baby animals born together.
examples: The cat had a litter.
A litter of puppies.
The litter was cute.

more.def: A group of young animals that are born at the same time to one mother.
examples: The cat had a litter of five kittens.
A litter of puppies slept in the box.
The farmer counted the litter.

easy.def: Not big.
examples: I have a little dog.
A little bird sat there.
She is a little girl.

more.def: Small in size or amount, or young.
examples: A little mouse squeezed through the tiny hole in the wall.
There is only a little milk left in the jug.
When I was little, I loved to play in the sandbox.

easy.def: To have your home in a place.
examples: I live in a house.
Fish live in water.
She lives near me.

more.def: To have your home in a place, or to make your home there.
examples: My grandparents live in a small town by the sea.
Polar bears live in the cold Arctic.
We lived in an apartment before we got a house.

easy.def: To be alive.
examples: Plants live and grow.
A turtle can live a long time.
We live and learn.

more.def: To be alive, or to stay alive.
examples: Some turtles live for more than a hundred years.
Plants need light and water to live.
He lived a long and happy life.

easy.def: The way you earn money to live.
examples: Fishing is his livelihood.
Farming is a livelihood.
Her livelihood is teaching.

more.def: The job or the way that a person earns money to pay for food and other things they need.
examples: Fishing is the livelihood of many people in the village.
His livelihood depends on the weather.
Farming has been her family's livelihood for generations.

easy.def: Full of energy.
examples: The puppy is lively.
The music was lively.
A lively game of tag.

more.def: Full of energy, life and excitement.
examples: The puppy was lively and ran around the yard.
The band played lively music for the dance.
We had a lively talk about the best way to build the fort.

easy.def: A body part that helps clean your blood.
examples: The liver is in your belly.
Your liver cleans blood.
The doctor talked about the liver.

more.def: An organ in your body that cleans your blood and helps you digest food.
examples: The liver is a large organ in your belly.
Your liver helps clean your blood.
A healthy diet is good for your liver.

easy.def: Farm animals like cows and sheep.
examples: The farmer has livestock.
Cows are livestock.
The livestock ate hay.

more.def: Animals that are kept on a farm for food, wool or work, such as cows, sheep and pigs.
examples: The farmer fed the livestock before sunrise.
Cows, sheep and pigs are livestock.
The fence keeps the livestock in the pasture.

easy.def: Very angry.
examples: He was livid.
She looked livid.
Dad was livid.

more.def: Extremely angry; or a gray-blue color from a bruise.
examples: He was livid when someone broke his toy.
She was livid about the mess.
The coach was livid at the referee's call.

easy.def: A small reptile with four legs and a long tail.
examples: The lizard sat on a rock.
A lizard is fast.
The lizard has a long tail.

more.def: A small reptile with a long body, four legs and a long tail.
examples: The lizard sunned itself on a rock.
A lizard darted across the path.
Some lizards can change color.
